articles.summary: It appears that tensions between Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb and Los Angeles Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson boiled over after the Bills' 37-34 victory on Monday Night Football.
articles.body:
It appears that tensions between Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb and Los Angeles Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson boiled over after the Bills' 37-34 victory on Monday Night Football .

Chubb and Jackson had a post-game confrontation that ended with Jackson punching Chubb in the face. Chubb was later seen having to be restrained by teammates as he continued to go after Jackson.

The altercation appeared to catch Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen's attention during a postgame interview:

Despite the testy altercation being caught on video, Chubb downplayed the situation while speaking to reporters after the game.

"It's just emotions, you know what I mean? Emotional game. It was a close game," Chubb said, per ESPN's Sarah Barshop . "And, you know, they always catch the second guy. So, I let him swing. And then my teammates held me back, and I just chilled."

Jackson was exchanging jerseys with Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker when it appeared Chubb said something to him to spark the brouhaha. Rams tight end Colby Parkinson pulled Jackson away after he threw the punch.

"Like I said, it was an emotional game. Tempers got flared," Chubb said. "But it is what it is. We flushed it and we onto next week."

When asked if Jackson's punch connected, Chubb replied, "I'm just ready for next week. … You see, I'm smiling, I'm with my team. … I'll be ready for next week."

It seems like Chubb is content to move on after helping the Bills outlast the Rams in overtime to improve to 4-1 this season. Buffalo will face the Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) on the road in Week 6.

articles.title: 'Pissed,' Sean McVay Sounds Off on Rams' Devastating OT Loss to Josh Allen, Bills
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay expressed frustration following his team's 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay expressed frustration following his team's 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night.

Speaking to reporters after falling short in a thrilling home game, McVay said, "This stinks. It's gonna hurt, but we can't let this team beat us twice. We're gonna have to regroup and reset ourselves. It's been a while since I've been this pissed after a game too."

Report Card Grades for Bills' in Dramatic Win ✏️

After falling behind 34-27 on a touchdown run by Bills running back James Cook with 1:39 left in regulation, the Rams offense moved quickly down the field, culminating in a game-tying touchdown run by Kyren Williams with five seconds remaining.

Cook lost a fumble on the first possession of overtime, meaning L.A. needed only a field goal to win the game. However, kicker Harrison Mevis' potential game-winning, 48-yard field goal was blocked by Greg Rousseau.

Buffalo then got into field goal range and won it with a 45-yard field goal from Tyler Bass.

After the game McVay said the Rams' extra point and field goal unit was "not even close to good enough" on Monday night and "cost us the game."

McVay added that he was going to "evaluate everything," which suggests some changes could be in store for the Rams' special teams unit.

With Monday's loss, the Rams fell to a surprising 2-3 on the season despite entering the campaign as the clear Super Bowl favorite.

Meanwhile, Buffalo improved to 4-1 with a resilient victory, and quarterback Josh Allen won the first overtime game of his career on his eighth try, counting playoffs.

The Rams will undoubtedly hope that welcoming in the 1-4 Arizona Cardinals next Sunday will help them get back on track with a victory following Monday's disappointing defeat.

articles.title: Woody Marks and the Best Week 6 Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups
articles.summary: With Week 6 on the horizon, the 2026 fantasy football season is approximately a third of the way through. It's becoming quite clear which teams have the inside track to make a championship run and which are facing uphill battles to even reach the postseason.
articles.body:
With Week 6 on the horizon, the 2026 fantasy football season is approximately a third of the way through. It's becoming quite clear which teams have the inside track to make a championship run and which are facing uphill battles to even reach the postseason.

However, there is still plenty of time for the landscape to shift before the playoff race truly heats up.

Injuries have been a major storyline during this fantasy campaign, with a variety of ailments sending an inordinate number of the NFL's top stars to the sidelines.

Because of the toll these injuries are taking, the true title contenders may not be the squads with the top full-strength starting lineup, but those with depth to withstand the loss of several key players.

The beginning of bye weeks represents another obstacle for managers to tackle. While only two teams were out last week, the many fantasy-relevant talents who play for the Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins and Minnesota Vikings will all be on break in Week 6.

Whether you need a one-week streamer to fill in for one of your usual starters or a longer-term replacement for an injured star, you'll be able to find plenty of suitable options in the free-agent pool.

With that in mind, let's look at the top waiver-wire pickups for Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season.

Suggestions are available in approximately half or more of all Yahoo! Sports leagues. Fantasy points and rankings courtesy of FantasyPros' PPR data. Suggested free-agent acquisition budget (FAAB) bids are based on a $100 starting budget.

Jameis Winston, New York Giants (6 Percent Rostered)

Winston has rapidly developed into a highly viable fantasy asset. While he didn't look prepared to be Big Blue's starter in Week 3, he turned things around and is now coming off a pair of top-eight finishes.

The veteran has legitimate QB1 upside for the remainder of the 2026 season.

While the gunslinging signal-caller will have his turnover troubles and accuracy issues—he tossed a pair of interceptions against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 4 and lost a fumble to the Washington Commanders this past week—that same high-risk play style also leads to plenty of fantasy points.

Winston is averaging 21 points over his past four starts dating back to last season. To put that in perspective, only four quarterbacks averaged more points during the 2025 campaign.

Although he won't put up week-winning numbers every start, Winston is the best free-agent choice for Week 6 and even has season-saving upside for managers who are truly desperate for a QB upgrade.

Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh Steelers (27 Percent Rostered)

After a shaky start to his 22nd season, Rodgers has locked in and put together his best fantasy stretch in years.

In the wake of his 22-point outing against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, Rodgers has now ripped off three consecutive QB12 or better finishes.

One would have to go back to the 2021 campaign—the most recent of the future Hall of Famer's four NFL MVP seasons—to find the last time he went on that type of streak.

The upcoming showdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers represents one of Rodgers' tougher tests of the season—the Bucs are only allowing an average of 14 fantasy points per game to opposing signal-callers—but any manager needing to stream the QB position in Week 6 shouldn't hesitate to fire up the 42-year-old.

Fernando Mendoza, Las Vegas Raiders (5 Percent Rostered)

Mendoza finally made his highly anticipated NFL debut late in the Raiders' blowout loss to the New England Patriots.

While he didn't move the needle much, the Indiana product completed a respectable six of eight throws for 48 yards and added three more yards on a lone rushing attempt.

Kirk Cousins is expected to remain Vegas' starter despite his struggles and is even a solid streaming choice for a Week 6 clash against the Buffalo Bills, but managers in deep formats can consider stashing Mendoza now.

Cousins' leash may have been shortened significantly by the rookie's promising performance, opening the door for the No. 1 overall pick to take the reins if the veteran continues to stumble.

Woody Marks, Houston Texans (54 Percent Rostered)

Marks' disappointing sophomore season started to get back on track in Week 5 thanks to his 85-yard, 19-touch performance against the Tennessee Titans.

Although his usage had been inconsistent over the first month of play, the second-year back saw a major bump in volume after starter David Montgomery picked up a groin injury.

Montgomery is now considered week-to-week , opening the door for Marks to take control of the backfield up until Houston's Week 8 bye.

Despite the likelihood of becoming the platoon's clear leader for a stretch, Marks should only be considered a fringe RB3 for Week 6. He has the misfortune to come up against a ferocious Jacksonville Jaguars front that has limited opposing running backs to a league-leading 10.6 fantasy points per game this year.

Despite the tough matchup, Marks should still be your top waiver-wire target for Week 6. He not only has short-term volume-based upside during Montgomery's absence, but the starter's inefficiency in recent weeks also gives Marks ample opportunity to secure a larger rest-of-season role.

Kendre Miller, New Orleans Saints (7 Percent Rostered)

With starter Travis Etienne Jr. on the IR with a hamstring strain and veteran backup Alvin Kamara severely limited by a back issue, Miller has become the healthiest and most productive option left in the Big Easy.

While Miller only saw the field for 14 offensive snaps during Sunday's disappointing loss to the Minnesota Vikings, he made the most of them by turning in 30 yards and a touchdown on 10 totes. He vastly outperformed Kamara, who only mustered six total yards on his five touches.

Expect head coach Kellen Moore to ride the hot hand and make Miller a far larger part of his offensive game plan in Week 6.

If the Saints are going to snap their three-game losing skid, they'll need Miller to go off against a New York Giants defense that is allowing 17.5 points per game to opposing RBs in 2026.

Dameon Pierce, Philadelphia Eagles (2 Percent Rostered)

Pierce may have spent the first month of 2026 on Philadelphia's practice squad, but he's poised for a huge Week 6 role within an Eagles offense that is quickly running out of backfield options.

Superstar starter Saquon Barkley is still rehabilitating his hamstring, Tank Bigsby remains on IR after undergoing core muscle surgery and Will Shipley could reportedly miss multiple weeks after partially tearing his plantar fascia on Sunday.

That leaves Pierce, who mustered just 14 yards on 11 carries against the Jags this past weekend, as the top option against the Carolina Panthers.

Although working behind a patchwork offensive line isn't ideal, managers can expect a far better performance from Pierce against a soft Panthers front.

Carolina has given up an average of 23.3 points per game to opposing RBs, tied for the third-most in the league this season.

With so many backs out on bye this week, managers could do far worse than rolling the dice on Pierce having a breakout game.

Kimani Vidal, Los Angeles Chargers (2 Percent Rostered)

The Chargers' offense may be imploding during a miserable 0-5 start to the season, but Vidal has been one of the team's few bright spots.

Although his ceiling is still capped by his place in L.A.'s three-man backfield platoon, Vidal saw his heaviest usage of the season in Week 5. He amassed 57 yards and a touchdown on eight carries, putting on a far more efficient performance than that of starter Omarion Hampton (33 yards on 14 totes) and fellow backup Keaton Mitchell (11 yards on six carries).

While that showing isn't likely to result in Vidal taking the top spot in the Bolts' rotation, he should see enough volume to make a fantasy impact when his squad squares off with the Kansas City Chiefs this weekend.

Consider Vidal a high-risk, high-reward flex choice as the Chargers try to find a way to secure their first win of 2026.

Jordyn Tyson, New Orleans Saints (49 Percent Rostered)

Tyson's much-anticipated NFL debut has been delayed by a hamstring injury he suffered late in the preseason.

Although New Orleans' brass is taking a "patient, long-term approach" to the receiver's recovery, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Tyson could return as early as Week 7, with Week 9 potentially the "most logical" option.

Expect the No. 8 overall pick to make an instant impact when he does get on the field, sliding right into a fantasy-relevant role as the Saints' No. 2 WR behind superstar Chris Olave.

While managers will have to wait a few more weeks to see returns on this waiver claim, that patience should be rewarded with a starting-caliber receiver who can put up big numbers in the back half of the season.

Germie Bernard, Pittsburgh Steelers (1 Percent Rostered)

With several Pittsburgh pass-catchers sitting out or hobbled by injury, Bernard more than adequately filled the void.

He finished a 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts with six catches and 80 receiving yards on nine targets. No other Steelers wideout recorded more than three catches, 12 receiving yards or four targets in the contest.

Head coach Mike McCarthy recently raved about the second-rounder's development, stating : "[Bernard has] acclimated very well to the offense, can play all three positions, and sticks his nose in there. I've been very impressed."

With that vote of confidence and a clear need for someone to step in this receiving corps, expect Bernard to become a larger part of Pittsburgh's plans each week.

Kendrick Bourne, Arizona Cardinals (3 Percent Rostered)

Bourne was already Arizona's No. 2 WR in terms of volume over the first four weeks, but he just had one of his best games yet with Marvin Harrison Jr. sidelined while awaiting his trade to the Houston Texans to be finalized.

Bourne finished the Cardinals' 21-45 loss to the Detroit Lions with five catches, eight targets and a team-high 70 receiving yards.

Although his floor is low—he was held without a target in Week 4—he has notched top-25 finishes in two of the first five games and should only see more looks with Harrison out of the picture.

Bourne is worth an add as a bye week and injury fill-in who can pad out your squad's depth.

Efton Chism III, New England Patriots (1 Percent Rostered)

Chism has a chance to become the next unheralded, diminutive slot receiver to thrive in New England.

With injuries taking their toll on the Patriots' receiving corps, he stepped up and became a hero with his game-winning touchdown catch against the rival Buffalo Bills in Week 4.

Chism followed that up with a steady five-catch, 57-yard Week 5 outing and has plenty of momentum going into this week's matchup with the New York Jets.

While he could fade back into irrelevance upon the eventual return of Mack Hollins and A.J. Brown, the wideout is worth a look and could pay massive dividends if he carves out a stable role in New England's offense.

Hunter Henry, New England Patriots (52 Percent Rostered)

Henry landed on the free-agent scrapheap in many leagues after he mustered a meager 71 yards on seven catches over the first three weeks of the 2026 campaign.

Cutting ties was understandable at the time, but two straight games with double-digit fantasy points makes him worth rostering again.

The New England tight end just wrapped up his best performance of the season, tallying 13.4 fantasy points against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Henry reeled in three of his four looks for 44 yards and scored his first TD of 2026 in the contest. That came on the heels of a five-target, five-catch, 62-yard performance that helped his Pats topple a tough Buffalo Bills opponent.

Even if you don't plan to utilize Henry as a weekly starter, he's still a fantastic streaming choice for Week 6. With the New York Jets on deck, the veteran is a strong bet to set more season-high marks.

Gang Green allows an average of 9.6 points per game to opposing TEs this year and gave up seven catches, 94 receiving yards and a score to Henry across two games last season.

Brenton Strange, Jacksonville Jaguars (16 Percent Rostered)

Strange didn't live up to his preseason sleeper status over the first three weeks of the season, but over the last two games, he's established himself as a critical piece of Jacksonville's offense.

Strange saw a season-high eight targets in Week 4, converting them into seven catches and 95 receiving yards. He received the same number of looks on Sunday, tallying another seven receptions in addition to 68 receiving yards.

Although Strange hasn't found paydirt since the opener, he's still on the TE1 radar following back-to-back top-10 finishes.

Unfavorable scheduling—which includes a battle with a tough Houston Texans defense in Week 6 before a Week 7 bye—prevents him from being a must-add waiver target, but he's still a fine investment for those seeking a long-term solution at the position.

Pat Freiermuth, Pittsburgh Steelers (15 Percent Rostered)

Freiermuth had his best outing of 2026 in Week 5, catching five passes for 44 yards and two touchdowns in Pittsburgh's 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts. The 21.5-point outing marked his first top-five finish of the campaign.

Although Freiermuth isn't putting up much yardage this season, he's averaging nearly four receptions per game and has four touchdowns in five contests. That pass-catching consistency and penchant for scoring gives him a respectable PPR floor that other waiver-wire tight ends lack.

Consider Freiermuth a low-upside, safe Week 6 streaming option against a Tampa Bay Buccaneers defense that has been allowing nearly 10 fantasy points per game to the TE position.

Darren Waller, Carolina Panthers (16 Percent Rostered)

Managers looking to gamble with their streaming tight end choice should look no further than Waller.

The boom-or-bust Carolina tight end is capable of massive fantasy performances due to his incredible scoring upside, but his inconsistent receiving production and a relatively low offensive snap share prevent him from emerging as a reliable starter.

Prior to Carolina's Week 5 bye, Waller recorded 13 receptions for 148 yards and two touchdowns on 19 targets. Although he averaged seven targets and four catches over his last two appearances, that workload figures to come down with the Panthers coming out of the break with a healthier crop of pass-catchers.

Waller will need to find the end zone against the Philadelphia Eagles to make a Week 6 fantasy start worthwhile.

articles.title: Week 6 Fantasy Football Rankings Overview for All Positions
articles.summary: Week 5 brought another slate of surprising results and even more surprising finishes. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers upset the Cowboys in Dallas to open the week, while the Baltimore Ravens capped Sunday by beating the Falcons in Atlanta in overtime without Lamar Jackson.
articles.body:
Week 5 brought another slate of surprising results and even more surprising finishes. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers upset the Cowboys in Dallas to open the week, while the Baltimore Ravens capped Sunday by beating the Falcons in Atlanta in overtime without Lamar Jackson.

Oh, and the New York Giants and Washington Commanders played to the first tie of the 2026 season.

The year has been filled with surprises so far, and that has been true for the fantasy football world, too. Bye weeks are not part of the uncertainty, and the Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins, and Minnesota Vikings will be off for Week 6.

Here, we'll dive into some early point-per-reception (PPR) rankings for the week, along with a few sleepers to consider plucking off the waiver wire at the key positions.

Waiver Target: Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas Raiders

The Las Vegas Raiders did bench quarterback Kirk Cousins for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza in Week 5, though they didn't do it for performance-based reasons. Things got out of hand in a blowout loss to the New England Patriots, so Mendoza got some playing time.

Cousins will be back under center when the Raiders host the Buffalo Bills this week. That makes him a terrific streaming option for managers who need a quarterback.

While Cousins tallied just 13.7 fantasy points in Week 5, he's topped 15 points in every other game this season, and he topped 20 points in Weeks 2-4. The Bills, meanwhile, allowed an average of 21.8 fantasy points to opposing QBs entering Monday night.

Cousins is rostered in just 48 percent of fantasy leagues.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Waiver Target: Dameon Pierce, Philadelphia Eagles

Dameon Pierce looms as a viable waiver target only because the Philadelphia Eagles are running out of other backfield options. Saquon Barkley is dealing with a hamstring injury, Tank Bigsby is on injured reserve, and Will Shipley suffered a foot injury on Sunday.

Pierce, who was signed from the practice squad to the active roster ahead of Week 5, recorded just 12 scrimmage yards on Sunday but saw 11 carries and two receptions. This week, he'll face a Carolina Panthers defense that ranks dead-last in yards per carry allowed (5.2).

Obviously, Pierce's value will take a hit if Barkley is able to return, but he's rostered in only two percent of fantasy leagues.

Waiver Target: Germie Bernard, Pittsburgh Steelers

Germie Bernard is another player who got an opportunity because of injuries in Week 5. The Pittsburgh Steelers rookie didn't make much of an impact during the early season, but he was heavily involved with Michael Pittman Jr. sidelined and with Roman Wilson suffering a finger injury on Sunday.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Wilson is expected to miss multiple weeks.

With Pittman and Wilson out, Bernard caught six of nine targets for 80 yards against the Indianapolis Colts. He'll next face a Buccaneers defense that ranks 20th in receiving yards allowed.

Bernard is rostered in just six percent of leagues.

Waiver Target: Brenton Strange, Jacksonville Jaguars

Brenton Strange has started to carve out a role in the Jacksonville Jaguars' offense, as opposing defenses have started focusing on receivers like Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers. He had minimal production in Weeks 2 and 3 but has reached double-digit fantasy points in back-to-back weeks.

This week, Strange will face a Houston Texans defense that hasn't exactly been friendly to opposing tight ends. However, Houston is likely to focus on slowing Jacksonville's wideouts, which could open opportunities for Strange.

The Jags' tight end should have a reasonable PPR floor this week, and he's still only rostered in 38 percent of fantasy leagues.

articles.title: Josh Allen Praises Matthew Stafford in Video After Bills-Rams, 'Greatest Thrower of the Football'
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen believes Los Angeles Rams signal-caller Matthew Stafford is the "greatest thrower of the football of all time" per a postgame interview with ESPN's Laura Rutledge following Buffalo's 37-34 road win over L.A. on Monday evening.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen believes Los Angeles Rams signal-caller Matthew Stafford is the "greatest thrower of the football of all time" per a postgame interview with ESPN's Laura Rutledge following Buffalo's 37-34 road win over L.A. on Monday evening.

"I've got an unbelievable amount of respect for Matthew," Allen said. "The way he's played the game, the way he's always played it. He's as tough as they come. If he's not the greatest thrower of the football of all time, I don't know who is. He spins it. He's a competitor. He's a quarterback that every guy should strive to be like."

The 38-year-old Stafford, who is in his 18th NFL season, completed 40-of-54 passes for 383 yards and three touchdowns.

Stafford put on a clinic, connecting with Puka Nacua 17 times for 138 yards and a score and finding Davante Adams for two more touchdowns (alongside his five catches for 51 yards). The Rams sorely needed his arm on a night where the running game didn't really get going (77 yards on 23 carries—3.3 yards per carry).

Buffalo's rushing attack did catch fire, with James Cook and Allen combining for 232 rushing yards and three touchdowns. So the Rams needed Stafford to keep pace.

Stafford delivered, and it looked like his efforts would be enough for a win when the Rams lined up for a game-winning 48-yard field goal attempt in overtime. However, Bills linebacker Gregory Rousseau blocked the kick, and Allen led Buffalo downfield for their own game-winning field goal.

It's a tough loss for the 2-3 Rams, but they can take solace in Stafford's ability to go blow-for-blow with anyone and keep the Rams in games. The reigning NFL MVP is arguably playing the best ball of his career after throwing for a career-high 4,707 yards and 46 touchdowns last year.

He's endured a tough schedule so far (the Rams' first five opponents have combined for a 17-7-1 record) but ranks second in the league in passing yards per game (314.4).

One can certainly make a case he's one of the NFL's best throwers of all time. Candidates include Aaron Rodgers, Dan Marino, John Elway and Patrick Mahomes, among others.

Allen is clearly a huge Stafford fan, though, after watching him Monday.

articles.title: Rams on Wrong Side of NFL History With Rare Stat From Heartbreaking Loss to Josh Allen, Bills
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams made history on Monday night, but not in the manner they would have liked.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams made history on Monday night, but not in the manner they would have liked.

In losing 37-34 in overtime to the Buffalo Bills, according to OptaStats, the Rams became the first team in NFL history to reach several significant benchmarks in the same game, only to lose:

Under head coach Sean McVay, the Rams did almost everything right offensively on Monday in what was a back-and-forth contest the entire way.

Quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 383 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, and wide receiver Puka Nacua had 17 receptions for 138 yards and a score.

Collectively, L.A. racked up 454 yards of total offense and 33 first downs, while not turning the ball over, compared to two turnovers for Buffalo's offense.

Despite that, the Rams needed a last second-score to force overtime, as a Kyren Williams rushing touchdown with five seconds remaining in regulation tied the game at 34-34.

In OT, the Bills got the ball first, but running back James Cook lost a fumble, meaning the Rams needed only a field goal to win.

However, Harrison Mevis' potential game-winning kick from 48 yards out was blocked by Greg Rousseau, leading to Tyler Bass' game-winning, 45-yard field goal for Buffalo.

The Rams' defense left plenty to be desired Monday night, allowing 436 yards of total offense, including 121 rushing yards and a touchdown to Bills quarterback Josh Allen, and 111 rushing yards and two touchdowns to Cook.

However, special teams were the Rams' primary undoing, as they missed both of their field goal attempts and allowed a 70-yard kick return by Ray Davis.

With the shocking home loss, the Rams dropped to 2-3 on the season, and desperately need to bounce back next weekend against the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: Puka Nacua Says Rams Need to 'Look at Ourselves in the Mirror' After 2-3 Start to 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: After falling to 2-3 following Monday night's overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills, the Los Angeles Rams don't appear to be the Super Bowl favorites that many pegged them to be entering the 2026 campaign.
articles.body:
After falling to 2-3 following Monday night's overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills, the Los Angeles Rams don't appear to be the Super Bowl favorites that many pegged them to be entering the 2026 campaign.

Despite the team's rocky start to the season, Rams star receiver Puka Nacua maintained his optimism as he looked ahead to the Week 6 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals (1-4).

"We've got to physically and mentally reset by tomorrow and get ready to play back here at home. ... It's going to be an opportunity to respond, really look at ourselves in the mirror and say what our identity is going to be," Nacua told reporters.

Nacua had one of the most dominant performances of his career in Monday's game, finishing with 17 catches for 138 yards and a touchdown. However, it wasn't enough, as the Bills secured a 37-34 victory in front of disappointed fans at SoFi Stadium.

The Rams had a busy offseason headlined by the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett and the return of future Hall of Famer Aaron Donald. However, Donald has just six tackles and no sacks in his three appearances this season, and Garrett was placed on injured reserve after suffering a knee injury in Week 1.

On paper, Los Angeles has all the talent needed to make it to the Super Bowl, but the team has yet to establish itself as a true title contender during its rollercoaster start to the year.

The Rams will try to get back on track when they face the Cardinals, who are coached by former Los Angeles offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur.

articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Responds to Viral Video of Dak Prescott's Exchange With Heckler After Bucs Loss
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is content to let fans express their First Amendment rights, even if that means publicly showing their disapproval toward the team.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is content to let fans express their First Amendment rights, even if that means publicly showing their disapproval toward the team.

Following a Week 5 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, someone inside the AT&T Stadium tunnel can be heard saying "embarrassing" as Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott walked by.

Jones addressed the moment during his usual appearance on 105.3 The FAN in Dallas.

"It doesn't impact me at all. The driver in question was not an employee," he said (via The Athletic's Jon Machota ). "Fans can express themselves, and should express themselves. Whether he was our employee or not, he was a fan, it sounds like. So, I'm for our fans expressing themselves."

The optics certainly aren't great when a stadium staffer — third-party contractor or not — makes such a visible show of their dissatisfaction in front of a player. But Jones has been pretty consistent when it comes to outside assessments of the team's performance.

He doesn't go out of his way to stifle dissent. The Cowboys' official site routinely provides clear-eyed analysis, even if that means calling out individual players or mistakes.

Veterans with as much tenure as Prescott know the lay of the land by this point. Playing for America's Team heightens both the praise and criticism.

When it comes to the latter, Jones will let the critics have their say.

articles.title: Cowboys Predicted to Win NFC East by NFL HC After 'Legit' Mike Pettine Hired to Staff
articles.summary: After the Dallas Cowboys hired veteran NFL coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant, some around the league feel that they have drastically changed their season outlook.
articles.body:
After the Dallas Cowboys hired veteran NFL coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant, some around the league feel that they have drastically changed their season outlook.

Cowboys insider Ed Werder spoke to a head coach who had Pettine on his staff, and the coach predicted that the Cowboys are now the favorites to win the NFC East.

"They finally hired a real coach. Pettine is legit. Dallas will walk away with that division now," the coach told Werder.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced on Monday that Pettine is being brought in to work with defensive coordinator Christian Parker. The 60-year-old is expected to play a major role in helping to turn around a defense that ranks 31st in yards allowed through the first five weeks of the season. Dallas gave up 419 yards to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers in their 24-16 loss on Thursday Night Football .

While Pettine will be assisting Parker, Werder noted that the power dynamics could shift at some point, as some NFL coaches told him, "The more influence and responsibility Pettine has, the better for the team."

Of note, Parker will now be moving to the coaching booth:

The Cowboys (2-3) will be hoping to see some improvements following Pettine's arrival when they take on the Green Bay Packers (3-2) on Sunday Night Football in Week 6.

articles.title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 6
articles.summary: Nick’s Power Rankings heading into Week 6
articles.body:
The 49ers keep rolling after an impressive road win in Seattle. Mike Evans went OFF, catching seven passes for 113 yards and a touchdown while battling through rib injuries. His addition has provided the Kyle Shanahan offense with a much-needed outside threat who is playing unreal late in his career. The defense forced four turnovers, as the 49ers continue to dominate.

The New England Patriots came to play! The Bills' defense surrendered 405 yards in the game, but a late Josh Allen interception, followed by a 12-yard Hunter Henry catch on third-and-10, secured the victory for New England. The 49ers jump the Bills here, but Buffalo is still a top-three team in the NFL.

The Chiefs were on their BYE, but still have persistent questions about their weapons on offense after the injury to Tyquon Thornton last week. Still, they're finding ways to win, have Patrick Mahomes, and Steve Spagnuolo's defense is playing well.

The Vikings defense continues to be elite. They held the Saints to 142 yards and Tyler Shough to 96 passing yards. Aaron Jones rushed for 113 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries, while Kyler Murray threw for 211 yards with a dime to Justin Jefferson. The Vikings offense is getting by, but the defense has carried them to an undefeated record through five weeks.

The Rams lost a heartbreaker in overtime, 37-34. Josh Allen did Josh Allen things at the end of the game. Both Allen and James Cook rushed for over 100 yards in the game. Matt Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns, while Puka Nacua caught 17 balls for 138 yards. Rams have three losses, but they're still a top team in the NFL.

Seattle turned the football over four times against the 49ers, who were all over Sam Darnold. Seattle could not stop Mike Evans. Sure, Seattle has two losses, but they're still a top team in the league.

Cam Little's last-second field goal let Jacksonville steal a win in London, where they'll play the Texans next week. Parker Washington played very well in the win and was the solution for Liam Coen's offense against an Eagles offense that has no identity.

Baltimore closed out a tight game with a nice comeback win over the Atlanta Falcons. Tyler Huntley did what he had to in the 30-23 victory. Baltimore should be receiving Lamar Jackson back either this week or the next.

New England is back?! The Patriots destroyed the Las Vegas Raiders at home, 45-17, which likely made Josh McDaniels smile. Drake Maye threw for 374 yards in the win. The Patriots defense SHUT down the Raiders' rushing attack and has stabilized over the past two weeks.

The Bears were embarrassed by the Green Bay Packers, 31-7. It was bad; Tyson Bagent couldn't do much offensively, but it was the Chicago defense that could NOT stop Jordan Love and the Packers' passing offense. Case Keenum moved the offense a bit, but it wasn't enough. A game to forget for the Bears, but it sets up well for the rematch between Matt LaFleur and Ben Johnson in Week 16.

The Bengals escaped Miami with a 31-24 win. Miami scored two fourth-quarter touchdowns, which made the game look more respectable, but it was Joe Burrow who threw four touchdowns, despite just 190 total yards on 23 completions. Miami did, however, gain 331 total yards and turned the football over three times, while rushing for 217 total yards, 74 of which were by quarterback Malik Willis.

Detroit dropped 45 on the Cardinals in the desert, beating Arizona 45-21. Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 151 yards on 25 carries and two touchdowns, and the Lions offense looked like what we're used to seeing. Jared Goff added three passing touchdowns.

Carolina was on a BYE, but moved up one spot in the rankings!

The Pittsburgh Steelers established the run well with Jaylen Warren, who had 101 yards on 15 carries with a touchdown. Aaron Rodgers threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Steelers' 34-22 win against the Colts.

The Broncos won a divisional matchup on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers, but their offense still doesn't look right under Sean Payton. Their defense is a top unit in the league, but Bo Nix and the offense have struggled. Denver had 224 total yards, with Nix throwing for just 123 yards. Still, a win is a win.

The Raiders were embarrassed by the Patriots and not much went right for Kirk Cousins and Klint Kubiak. We did see, however, Fernando Mendoza, who went 6 of 8 for 48 yards in garbage time. Las Vegas did nothing on the ground against this Patriots front; Asthon Jeanty had 27 yards on 10 carries.

The Packers have three wins despite this season going TERRIBLY so far. But, WOW, did the Packers' offense turn on against the Bears' defense: a 31-7 win where Jordan Love threw for 367 yards and two touchdowns. MarShawn Lynch rushed for a pair of touchdowns as well, while only averaging 3.1 yards per carry.

The Giants tied the Washington Commanders, 27-27, and they had the win in their hands but missed a field goal and fumbled it away; but the Commanders also did not want to win the football game, which led to one of the wilder endings I've ever covered. The Giants may look to spread things out and operate out of the shotgun with Jameis Winston, for it's obvious he's more comfortable letting it sling, rather than operating a heavy play action passing attack that can't run the ball anyway.

Atlanta lost in overtime at home to a backup quarterback — not ideal! Still, the Ravens are a well-coached team, and perhaps the game ends differently if Tua Tagovailoa wasn't forced into action. Michael Penix Jr. perhaps doesn't throw the game-sealing interception. Still, Atlanta lost the game, but they're better than their 2-3 record would suggest.

Dallas was beaten by a backup quarterback on Thursday Night Football. The Buccaneers dominated for much of the game, despite a late push by Dak Prescott. The final score was 24-16; Christian Parker's defense has been an abject disaster, as Bucky Irving rumbled for 165 yards and a touchdown on the ground.

The Texans beat up on the Tennessee Titans, 26-3. C.J. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a touchdown, but the Texans lost David Montgomery to an injury in the game. I don't like having the Texans this high, but, like the Falcons, they've underperformed and failed to finish close games against solid opponents earlier in the season.

The Cleveland Browns fell to the Jets, 17-12, at MetLife Stadium. Braelon Allen ran for 116 yards and a touchdown in the game, as Garrett Wilson caught seven passes for 104 yards with a score against the Browns, who could not get much going on offense.

The Eagles are a mess offensively, as they lost in a last-second field goal against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Even though the Eagles are beat up on the offensive line, they're trading Pro Bowl offensive linemen. Still, their defense is a solid unit, but the team is lost right now.

Daniel Jones threw for 267 yards against Pittsburgh, but the Colts did little on the ground, as the Steelers rolled to a 34-22 win. Jonathan Taylor averaged just three yards per carry. Indianapolis went 4 of 15 on third down, and the Colts turned the football over on downs twice in the fourth quarter.

Washington was a disaster in that end-of-game situation. Getting Jayden Daniels back is huge for Washington, but the Giants' defense shut down the offense —for the most part. Daniels, though, has to do a better job at the end of the game to secure that victory.

The Jets offense was much better in their Week 5 win against the Cleveland Browns. They won 17-12, scoring 10 points in the fourth quarter to seal the victory. New York had 276 yards on offense on 65 plays, up from 32 last week.

The Saints couldn't do anything against the Vikings at home. Brian Flores will do that.

The Buccaneers pulled off an upset on Thursday Night Football as they await Baker Mayfield's return. The Buccaneers' defense stifled the Dallas offense. The Buccaneers have an uphill battle, but the NFC South is still open.

Arizona surrendered 45 points to the Detroit Lions. They couldn't stop Gibbs and did not do much offensively to challenge the Lions, although Trey McBride had a WILD touchdown grab.

The Chargers remain winless. Their offense is an absolute mess, and Justin Herbert looked lost against the Broncos. He was sacked five times; neither offense played well in the game, but the Chargers are the league's biggest disappointments through five weeks.

Miami made the score against the Bengals look respectable, but Cincinnati controlled the game. Still, this is — at least — the second consecutive game where the Dolphins kept it…interesting. Ollie Gordon had another solid outing too.

The Texans dismantled Tennessee, and the team remains winless and has struggled offensively.

articles.title: Eli Manning pinpoints a flaw he noticed in Josh Allen’s play despite Bills win over Rams
articles.summary: Former quarterback Eli Manning has been breaking down Josh Allen’s game on the back of the Buffalo Bills’ meeting with the Los Angeles Rams. The Bills secure...
articles.body:
Former quarterback Eli Manning has been breaking down Josh Allen's game on the back of the Buffalo Bills' meeting with the Los Angeles Rams.

The Bills secured a late victory on Monday, with Allen managing to pick up his first-ever overtime win in the NFL.

The quarterback shone on the night, but Manning is of the opinion that the 30-year-old should start taking the easier option during plays.

Eli Manning says Josh Allen 'won't always take the open guy'

Speaking about the NFL on ESPN, he explained: "Sometimes Josh he has guys open but he doesn't always throw it.

"You know he kind of has the quick out right here to the right to Coleman. You can throw that and he can turn up and hit the first down.

"Sometimes because he has such, the ability to scramble and make plays, he kind of won't always take the open guy."

He added: "Just because you have the ability to scramble, we can still get the ball out on time a little bit more."

While Allen's game may not be completely perfect in the eyes of Manning, he is having a terrific 2026/27 so far.

He has managed 1,249 passing yards with a 65.9 percent completion rate and an average of 9.1 per attempt, which is the third-best average in the league behind Michael Penix Jr. (9.3) and Lamar Jackson (10.1).

articles.title: NFL Draft stock report- hold: Dylan Raiola, QB, Oregon
articles.summary: As brutal as it may have been, it's only one game, and taking accountability is the first step towards making improvements.
articles.body:
The backup quarterback made his first start in an Oregon Ducks uniform on Saturday, as QB1 Dante Moore remains sidelined after sustaining a nasty, cheap shot by a USC defender a couple of weeks ago. Moore is still recovering from concussion related injuries, so Raiola was QB1, until he wasn't.

The former five star recruit got benched in the Ducks' 17-15 loss to UCLA. Raiola threw two interceptions, against only six completions (in 19 attempts), for just 43 yards on 31.6 percent completion.

His yards-per-pass was a laughably low 2.3 which almost matched his QBR (of 2.4), which was so awful, you might have thought that this number was a typo at first.

The Nebraska transfer was then benched in favor of third-stringer Brock Thomas. Credit Raiola though, for actually meeting with the media after the game. Quarterback is the most scrutinized and over-analyzed position in all of sports, by far. Most QBs, after having performed that egregiously awful, would not go and face the music directly afterward.

He actually did, and that showed maturity.

"I owe the respect to you guys," Raiola answered, when asked why he met with the media in postgame. "I owe the respect to the fans and everybody that's incorporated with this thing."

"I've got a younger brother, and he looks up to me.

"I mean, this isn't just football, this is life, and tough situations happen. You gotta own them. There's no running around 'em. There's no dodging 'em. The product we put out there — the product I put out there — I gotta live with that. I gotta own everything, take it on the chin, and move forward. We've got a quick turnaround."

The fact that he showed up and took accountability for his dreadful game is why we're rating him "Hold" instead of "Sell" or even "Strong Sell."

As brutal as it may have been, it's only one game, and taking accountability is the first step towards making improvements. Raiola transferred in knowing that he would be Moore's back-up this year, and that he would then be the alpha dog in 2027.

He's a 2028 draft prospect, not a 2027. Also, while his 2024 season was statistically mid, his 2025 season was statistically stellar, so we've seen mixed results so far.

Raiola may not be living up to the 5-star hype as of yet, but you can't call him a bust either. No, it did not really work out in Lincoln, but he still has all the potential to develop into a star someday.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Film Review: 5 things that stood out to Hayden Winks from Week 5
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks enters the Week 5 film room.
articles.body:
Fantasy football is inundated with stats and charts (guilty!!!), but the more context the film provides, the more reliable the data gets. That's why we have a 2.5-hour show called Stats vs. Film every Tuesday at 6 p.m. EST. That show is live — join us in the chat!!!

This (experimental) weekly column will look at some of the biggest storylines I picked up by grinding the film.

Ashton Jeanty is not playing fast enough

His ankle and foot injury partially explains this, but this was Jeanty's primary problem as a rookie, too. Jeanty's particular issue is quickly changing direction and bursting through the hole or away from a space defender. This isn't overly surprising, as it's uncommon for the elite RB prospects to skip NFL Combine testing, and Jeanty did just that.

Compared to the elite RBs, Jeanty's processing is forgettable. The play above is an example of not seeing things well. We have an inside zone run, where the C is going to climb to the LB after engaging with the DT. Jeanty doesn't trust it, stutters his feet and misses a potential window to hit the hole.

This is another missed read, this time on a power run. Jeanty should be trailing his pulling guard and waiting for him to block the LB. Instead, Jeanty is impatient and bounces it towards Brock Bowers, who lost his matchup. There is a hole up in the middle if he finds it. On man and power runs this year, Jeanty is averaging 3.0 yards per carry.

Some of this absolutely falls on the Raiders OL not getting enough push on their individual blocks. The lack of yards before contact (0.6) this season is not dissimilar to what happened last year. Unfortunately, the more we learn about yards before contact, the more we learn that the RB has more say in it than originally given credit for.

Here are the bottom 10 RBs in yards before contact this season, and it's not a coincidence that they are the slowest RBs in the NFL:

My last note on Jeanty is as a receiver. He's very capable on option routes and the occasional downfield route, but he's simply dropped too many passes, particularly over the middle on fast balls from Kirk Cousins. The Raiders might be trying to evaluate exactly how they can use him in the pass game because his protection has included multiple pretty fatal reps. Dylan Laube was playing a lot more than usual last week, limiting Jeanty to 53% snaps in the first half. Some of that is the injury, but some of that is because he's not an elite bellcow back.

Jeremiyah Love looked healthier than his box score

Following a new right ankle sprain in Week 4, Love managed to get in a full practice heading into Sunday. He started, played in the 2-minute drill and started the second half before being shelved in a dead fourth quarter. He totally busted in the box score, but how did he look?

There was a wild jump over a blocker, many quick cuts and enough reps of him getting up to speed to believe he can be productive if the Cardinals allow it. Where the tape was concerning was across the OL. They don't have starting LT Parris Johnson Jr. for the rest of the year, and the rest of the OL has been problematic all season. There simply wasn't a lot of room to run in Week 5 against the Lions.

Love was on the field for the goal-line play-action rep before garbage time, so there might be a little more value in this role than what we saw last week in REAL garbage time. The comments around Love's happiness and health are concerning, but the Cardinals are going to get real desperate here.

Beyond his health, the consistent thing on his film is he's been a little too jumpy/dancy. He's a very explosive player who can jump around defenders and find hidden holes, but there are other times where he's jumping around to nowhere. Finding that balance is what turns the good starters into the great ones.

Small sample noise can lead us astray, but Golden is just very good. It's as simple as that. There will be an occasional drop or miscommunication with Jordan Love given his experience, but Golden moves like the top downfield receivers in the NFL. His explosiveness at the line is obvious; he can maintain separation downfield, and he has springs at the catch point.

All of that manifested on this man-coverage rep against CB1 Jaylon Johnson:

You'll notice Jordan Love saw the matchup after peaking to Golden's side, checked out of the run and then launched it to him with perfect placement. Golden had an extremely similar rep up the seam, too.

Beyond this rep, Golden is adding multiple quick-hitting reps, like screens, slants, hitches and scramble-drill wins, so his floor is higher than others with this downfield ability. He's on pace for 80 receptions and 1,350 yards right now. If Love is going to have as much time in the pocket as he did last year after the Packers began moving around their starting offensive linemen, then this team can rip explosives with the best of them.

Love had six completions for 252 yards on passes over 20 air yards, both a single-game high this season. He also had a phantom OPI called back that would've made his stat 7-302-2.

Bernard is the consensus top waiver wire add of the week . The role is undeniable with Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on injured reserve, and Roman Wilson (finger) expected to be out multiple weeks. Bernard ran a route on 36 of 38 Week 5 dropbacks. That's enough to be an auto top-50 fantasy WR, but the question is, can he be a bye-week starter in fantasy?

In Week 2, Bernard had a bubble screen clank off his chest for a horrid interception, one that required Aaron Rodgers himself to make the tackle. I'm sure Rodgers loved that.

This week, Bernard had two other drops. Bernard's toughest drop began by not knowing the play. Once again as the flanker, Bernard began blocking for a run play and realized he had a route to run. He cut inside, just where Jaylen Warren was expected to be as the checkdown. Bernard sat right in front of Warren, then dropped it. That's what it's like playing as a rookie in a dense Rodgers offense.

His other one was the flanker in a trips set, running a seam ball against zone coverage after Rodgers drew an edge offside. While turning around, Bernard dropped a perfect pass that would've gone for an explosive. Drops happen, so this wasn't so bad.

The Steelers seem willing to live with the mistakes, and Rodgers has even spent pre-production time talking up his second-round rookie. I loved Bernard's versatility and toughness on his Alabama tape, so I do hope he can round out his game immediately. Bernard's positive plays in Week 5 reflected those traits. He had two slant wins in traffic, then two big-boy dig routes for chunk gains. Rodgers likes to throw these underneath passes into tight windows, and Bernard has the size and willingness to be targeted here.

Jaylen Warren is a star. There's no competition between him and Rico Dowdle. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.

Tyler Shough (left hand) had to hand the ball off only with his right hand. I wouldn't be surprised if his non-throwing hand is broken right now. Speaking of broken, the Saints have the worst RB and TE blocking rooms in the NFL. That's really what broke the Saints versus Brian Flores.

Many of Kyler Murray's biggest plays were a bit out of structure. His speed on scrambles was excellent and very valuable. There were also chunk passing gains in the scramble drill, and his big touchdown pass to Justin Jefferson was after he got bumped off his route. Even while he learns the feel of this new downfield offense, Murray's play-making is a fun backup plan. The Vikings are heading on bye now, and they could absolutely use it with their injuries.

Parker Washington is excellent. His physicality and ball skills have been evident since late last year. That showed up again when he peaked around the much-bigger Riq Woolen before extending his other hand for a one-handed TD. What I didn't realize was how fast he is in a straight line. His long, leaking TD showcased burst that is reminiscent of the top slot/flanker types, like Steve Smith Sr.. Washington is going to get the biggest bag at any moment.

Makai Lemon just might not be quick enough to be a difference maker. A quick slant covered by Travis Hunter was pretty glaring in terms of movement skills and length. There was another screen called for him that went incomplete because he initially went out to block. This isn't the first time that's happened this year, so don't be surprised if his snaps stagnate or reduce with Darius Cooper playing better and offering more in the run game. Lemon is droppable.

The Eagles had another 10 unblocked pressures (bad), but they attacked it differently this time around. They went empty to simplify things and often threw it downfield. Those went incomplete this time, but this was a better plan for Jalen Hurts when teams are blitzing. It's evident that they don't trust their fourth- and fifth-string RBs in protection, nor should they. The other thing with the new-look Eagles offense is a pivot away from the Tush Push. Neither of their one-yard-to-go plays were pushes, and their new C (who had some bad snaps) and extremely undersized new LG (who had five pressures allowed) aren't equipped to run it. That really hurts Hurts' fantasy value.

Tyler Warren is being utilized more downfield without Alec Pierce. In 17 games with Pierce, his aDOT is just 4.5 yards downfield. In seven games without Pierce involved, Warren's aDOT is up to 6.5 yards. Last week's 9.9 aDOT was the second highest of his career. He had a pair of wheel routes up the sideline, then more breaking routes in the 8-15 yard range. Those will be helpful for the next few weeks. A bonus FB dive at the goal line for a score is also helpful.
